What's inside

Three reasons to stop here

Tap any one of them to see what's behind it.

Sandwiches made to order, built while you wait. It's the one thing this stop has that the chains on the highway don't.

The made-to-order sandwiches are what reviewers single out.

An aisle that has no business being on this stretch of highway — imported instant noodles and Asian snacks, shelved right beside the chips.

The surprise nobody expects at this end of 410.

Drinks out the door, plus the everyday things you'd otherwise drive into town for. There's an ATM inside the door and EBT is taken at the register.

Who's behind the counter

A family, three shifts deep

Read the reviews of this store and almost nobody talks about the shelves. They talk about the people at the register.

A mom who jokes with customers and makes them feel welcome. A dad who is helpful and gets you moving. Their son, who regulars know too. Between them they cover a store that's unlocked before dawn and still lit long after dinner, seven days a week, on a highway where most of the traffic is only passing through.

That's a long day to be the friendly face on someone's commute, and it is the single thing customers come back to write about.

Getting here

Right on the highway

  1. Watch for the awning

    Long, salmon-pink, running the full width of the building with the green sign on it. You can see it from 410 in either direction.

  2. Call ahead for the deli

    Ordering a sandwich to grab on your way through? Ring the counter and it can be waiting.

  3. Pull in and park

    A full lot with marked stalls sits between the highway and the door, so you're never blocking a lane while you shop.

Thanks — someone at the counter will get back to you.
